subject_line: Naomi's detective turn, and the poems of Three Sides of a Coin
email_body:
Dear Joseph,

Reading about the 2023 Kistrech Poetry Festival, I noticed that the writer of Naomi the Detective, nominated for the Wahome Mutahi Prize, also has poems from Three Sides of a Coin translated into German and French. I'd love to ask how Naomi grew into a series, and whether your scholarly work on girl characters in children's books shaped how you wrote her.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Mzee Lelma and the stolen herd in Mourning Glory
email_body:
Dear Professor Kabaji,

I read Peter Amuka's review of Mourning Glory and keep thinking about Mzee Lelma, the herder left grieving after his livestock is stolen in the cattle rustling between Pokot and Turkana communities. Since you write in Maragoli and Kiswahili as well as English, I'd love to ask how you found the voice for an adult novel set so far from the children's books many readers know you for.

subject_line: Masks and the Ayaka masquerade across your novel and poems
email_body:
Dear Professor Orabueze,

Looking at your staff profile, I noticed masks recur across your writing: the novel Men Behind the Masks, published by Afro Orbis in Nsukka, and the poetry collection The Message of the Ayaka Masquerade and Other Poems. I'd love to ask whether that image came first in the poems or in the novel, and how writing fiction sits alongside your critical work in Society, Women and Literature in Africa.

subject_line: Writing The Misogynist and To The Stars in the same year
email_body:
Dear Dr Afolabi,

Your OAU Dramatic Arts profile notes that you published two plays in 2014, To The Stars and The Misogynist, both with Penthouse Publications in Ibadan, and that your plays are now taught at undergraduate and postgraduate level. I'd love to ask how directing and managing theatre at Ife shapes what you put on the page, and what it is like to see students study your own plays.
